description: Lesson 1-3 activity: user studies examples to distinguish bad/good/great ideas, then runs a rigorous brainstorm to generate a list of candidate ideas for their own talk and decides which to keep or cut, narrowing toward a single through-line.

exercise_name: Brainstorm and develop your talk idea list
description: User does a structured brainstorm to develop a written list of possible ideas for their talk, the core hands-on assignment of the 'Identify Your Ideas' section.
User curates brainstormed ideas down to a single connecting through-line for the talk, deciding which ideas to keep and which to cut.

exercise_name: Craft your talk plan (script vs improvise)
description: User builds a plan for their talk, deciding when to fully script and when to improvise/extemporize during delivery.
Lesson on using vocal delivery and body language/movement to strengthen the talk; user applies these techniques to rehearsing their own talk.
User learns and applies methods to build rapport and connect with the audience both in person and online while delivering their talk.
User learns narrative techniques and shapes their talk using the 'ancient art of storytelling' to make delivery more compelling.
User practices articulating sophisticated/complex ideas with clarity and accessibility within their talk.
User learns techniques to encourage the audience to genuinely consider their viewpoint, applying persuasion methods to their talk.
User explores dynamic ways to introduce and reveal the key concept/idea of the talk for maximum impact.
Final lesson: user learns effective vs ineffective use of visual aids/slides and applies it to their own talk.
Across the 11 lessons the user develops their own TED-style talk end to end (idea -> through-line -> plan -> delivery -> visuals); the cumulative deliverable is a finished talk the user can perform.

User delivers a full presentation (can bring their own slides/notes) to a simulated virtual audience, then fields follow-up questions from AI avatars in a live Q&A; avatars ask questions based on what the user just said.
User uploads slides and notes and rehearses a presentation in front of a realistic AI audience in a chosen venue, receiving delivery analytics afterward.
User discusses any topic with one or more simulated AI participants in a free-form conversation scenario.
User uploads a resume and job description; the AI generates role-tailored interview questions and the user practices answering with an AI interviewer.
User role-plays a hard interpersonal conversation (e.g., conflict resolution, leadership conversation, workplace investigation) with an AI persona whose pushback level can be tuned.
User rehearses a sales call, pitch, or client conversation against a simulated AI prospect/client persona.
User practices delivering a short elevator pitch to a virtual audience/persona.
User practices arguing a position in a debate-style scenario against an AI counterpart, in a debate venue.

exercise_name: Therapy session / medical exam / language tutoring roleplays
description: Specialized roleplay scenarios (e.g., conducting a therapy session, a medical exam, or a language-tutoring conversation) built on the same AI-persona engine; used for profession-specific or language practice.
Before practicing, user designs the AI character by setting its mood, background, language, tone, role, and level of pushback, then runs any scenario against that tuned persona.

User rehearses in one of ~14 lifelike venues (boardroom, classroom, lecture hall, conference hall, press conference, courtroom, stadium) with audience sizes scaling up to thousands of spectators to build pressure tolerance.

After any session the user reviews a full transcript plus delivery metrics (filler words, pacing, eye-contact/gaze distribution across the audience, mic distance) and customizable AI-generated coaching notes, tracking improvement over time.

User picks one of 12 topic categories (e.g., The Job Interview, The College Interview, Debate Team, Pop Culture Favorites, Speed Dating, Small Talk, At Work) and is served five prompts to speak to on the fly; the app listens via voice recognition and scores the response.

User speaks freely for up to 30 minutes to rehearse any presentation, interview, or audition; can choose which specific filler words the app tracks, pause/stop anytime, and gets a results breakdown at the end.

Real-time speech-fitness analysis that flags filler words ('like', 'ya know', 'so', 'actually', 'I mean', etc.) and measures pace (optimal ~150 wpm), producing an 'Articulate' letter grade from A+ to 'Uh Oh!' as the feedback mechanism on every session.

provider: Charisma Virtual Social Coaching (Center for BrainHealth, UT Dallas)
description: In a 3D virtual environment (Unreal Engine), the user navigates real-time social situations as an avatar, practicing skills like initiating conversations, maintaining relationships, managing interpersonal dynamics, and handling difficult social moments, with a live coach guiding.

provider: Charisma Virtual Social Coaching (Center for BrainHealth, UT Dallas)
description: Across 10 hours/sessions, a clinician teaches a set of social-cognitive strategies (research describes nine; the program frames them as Curiosity, Connection, Courage, Charisma pillars) and the user then practices each strategy in role-play, with live coaching interspersed between practice reps.

provider: Charisma Virtual Social Coaching (Center for BrainHealth, UT Dallas)
description: User practices starting and opening conversations with avatar partners in the virtual world, a core targeted skill of the protocol.

provider: Charisma Virtual Social Coaching (Center for BrainHealth, UT Dallas)
description: User role-plays sustaining a relationship and navigating interpersonal dynamics (e.g., reading emotions, responding appropriately) with avatars, building emotional intelligence.

provider: Charisma Virtual Social Coaching (Center for BrainHealth, UT Dallas)
exercise_name: Population-specific tracks (Transition to Adulthood, Children & Families)
description: Program variants tailor the role-play scenarios to specific life contexts (e.g., job/college/independent-living social situations for the Transition to Adulthood track), each delivered through the same coached virtual-practice model.
